event.summary: The wake timer bounds only the connection state at its expiry
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 533169cf19571d34af3a8497eaceb8d2d7b7c852. TLDR: A connection that becomes pending again after the wake timer has expired can leave the launch waiting without another 60-second limit. Considered whether the one-shot timer violates the promised bounded wake. Source: create_form.rs:7490-7522 starts one timer per woken_connection_wait value, checks the currently parked stamp, and does not rearm when connection state changes; :7530-7592 retains the continuation while awaiting_woken_connection is true. Contract: SPEC_impl.md:210-215 explicitly says, "The limit is checked when its 60 seconds run out: a press still waiting for a connection then is discarded, even one that saw the host connect and lost it again before that point, while a host that shows a connection pending again only after that point is not bounded by it." Suggested bucket: other if the contract were different; no established security or loss-of-work route. Could-be-highest: false. Confidence: confirmed from source, no execution. proposed_drop: explicit specification acceptance, exact text quoted above. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not searched. Caveat: this records the one-shot boundary only; it does not establish that a particular later reconnection remains pending indefinitely. No reproduction was performed.

event.summary: Retiring the container controls does not silently remove stored isolation
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc. TLDR: Considered whether removing the old container editor and destination eligibility checks lets a stored isolated setup launch directly on its host. That security consequence is not supported by the new source. Details: draft.rs:230-232 refuses any active Agent draft containing the retired configuration, :747-750 prevents structured_selection from projecting it as a launch, :1966-1977 refuses direct recent activation before draft/history changes, and :2651-2659 refuses recent search activation before destination adoption. create_form.rs:5864-5868 and :6832-6836 recheck container_refusal before launch preparation and after key minting. Template replay at create_form.rs:818-899 goes through farhelm-proto/src/launcher.rs:667-669, which returns RETIRED_CONTAINER_REASON for a stored container object. The raw configuration remains in the compatibility projection rather than becoming None. Contract: SPEC.md, Retired containerized sessions (:4816-4823), says stored choices still load but use drops or refuses the retired choice with an explanation and cannot create another old-style session. Suggested bucket if the suspected route existed: highest/security. Could-be-highest: true (loss of intended isolation), but the route is refuted by the explicit refusal and unprojectable structured selection. Confidence: confirmed from source, no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation; the suspected ordinary-host launch path is blocked at both draft projection and submit, and old template objects fail the shared template fold. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not searched. Caveat: dormant Agent configuration does not block the explicitly selected Command tab, consistent with the independent retained field groups; no claim is made about unrelated command-launch safety.

event.summary: Retired container objects are refused; modern environment targets are separate
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc. TLDR: The original suspected security consequence was a stored container-isolated setup silently launching directly on its host after removal of its editor. This remains refuted for retired ContainerConfig objects, and does not refute modern environment placement problems such as l1. Source: draft.rs:230-232 refuses active Agent drafts carrying container; :747-750 returns None for their structured_selection; :1966-1977 refuses direct recent activation before history/draft writes, and :2651-2659 refuses search recent activation before destination adoption. create_form.rs:5864-5868 and :6832-6836 check the refusal before launch and after key mint. Templates pass through the whole-fold check at create_form.rs:818-899; farhelm-proto/src/launcher.rs:667-669 rejects Some(Some(container)) with RETIRED_CONTAINER_REASON. The raw container is retained in editing_selection, preserving compatibility fingerprints. Contract, exact text at SPEC.md:4818-4823: 'The earlier experimental model, whose supervisor stayed outside the container and bind-mounted a host checkout, is retired.' Also: 'Templates, recent setups and history with that choice still load. Using them drops or refuses the retired choice with an explanation and cannot create another old-style session.' Suggested bucket for the original silent-isolation-removal claim: highest/security. Could-be-highest: true, original consequence preserved; explicit source refusals refute that route. Confidence: confirmed source analysis, no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation limited to retired container objects; no parent drop accepted. possible_cover: none for this candidate; the caller's g085/l2 and g086 report concerns modern entry.target, recorded separately in l1. Synthesis evidence: draft.rs is the identical blob 20ee6a92d0f51111336e6457d1fed7cd96229020 at all five assigned commits; the form's relevant retired-choice checks remain unchanged through f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. Caveats: Command is a separate explicitly selected draft group, so dormant Agent configuration is not a guard on arbitrary commands. Modern entry.target carries provider/place intent and normally has selection.container == None; the retired-object checks therefore do not prevent l1's modern recent mutation and do not certify all placement transitions as correct.

event.detail: Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc. TLDR: Considered whether the new retired-Recent test could pass through an unrelated ordinary-operation busy refusal while never exercising its new guard. Its own setup and error assertions distinguish that mechanism. Source: seed_placement_command at draft.rs:4835-4843 asserts admission of each concrete command/prompt/conversation edit, establishing an editable fixture. Initial composer_reset_reason is 'old reset' (:3793), and use_final_context initializes the search template_error to None (:3943). The test :8548-8620 first checks direct refusal and requires composer_reset_reason to contain 'Delete only'; only the new retired-container branch at :1966-1977 supplies that reason in this call. It then requires the separate search template_error to contain 'Delete only'; the direct call did not seed that slot, and a busy apply_edit return cannot populate it. The before snapshot is an executable Command draft while the offered ordinary Recent would switch to Agent and restore choices if accepted; whole-draft and retry-pair equality therefore distinguish forbidden application, not merely an unchanged compatible setup. Suggested bucket for the considered test-oracle gap: other, but no defect established. Could-be-highest: false; this candidate concerns maintainer test sensitivity only. Confidence: confirmed fixture/assertion/source analysis, no execution. proposed_drop: source refutation of busy-no-op false pass; production correctness alone was not used as a test-quality proof. possible_cover: none in supplied interface projection; no prohibited coverage-source search. Caveat: this test checks owner-operation refusal and does not claim to validate every rendered control or the connection timer. No new test deficiency or product behavior is inferred from those deliberate bounds.
